same_basis_candidates.why_it_applies: Nearest same-basis sovereign read-across, not direct coverage: EU 2024/1987 point 3.6.15 'baby food except juices', 0.50 mg/kg on product as placed on market (wet, as consumed), the only EU nickel row whose scope contains fish (meat- and fish-based baby foods); in force since 2025-07-01.
Swiss VHK mirror of the same baby-food row at 500 ug/kg as consumed; concurring second sovereign for the nearer read-across, not direct coverage of adult seafood.

cells.reason: No sovereign instrument in the register sets a nickel ML for fish, shellfish, cephalopods or any animal-tissue food, so this cell is a read-across whichever row is chosen; the test is which row is nearest. EU 2024/1987 point 3.6.11.3 'husked rice' (2.0 mg/kg, product as placed on market, a dry cereal at roughly 12-14 % moisture) is neither product-adjacent nor basis-adjacent to wet, as-consumed canned tuna and canned fish (drained fish content), and the same instrument's wet-basis rows all sit far lower: 'baby food except juices' 0.50 mg/kg (point 3.6.15, as placed on market, a category that includes meat- and fish-based baby foods and is the only EU nickel row whose scope contains fish), fruiting vegetables 0.40, brassica and leafy vegetables 0.50, root/tuber/bulb vegetables 0.90 and legume vegetables 1.0 (wet weight). The husked-rice row is in force (applies from 2026-07-01) but is not the nearest same-basis sovereign instrument; the nearer one is the baby-food row at 500 ug/kg (Switzerland VHK mirrors it at 500 as consumed), so the read-across as claimed is refuted and the blind value is 500.
